topStories.headline: Viz Valley Middle School Teachers Build Their Own Fundraising Nonprofit After Years Without a PTA
topStories.dek: Staff at Visitacion Valley Middle School have spent nine months organizing Friends of Viz Valley, a teacher-led nonprofit designed to fill the fundraising gap that a missing PTA has left at one of southeast San Francisco's most under-resourced schools.
topStories.body:
Teachers and staff at Visitacion Valley Middle School have launched a new nonprofit called Friends of Viz Valley after recognizing the school had no Parent-Teacher Association and no structured way to raise money for programs its roughly 300 students need. The group spent the better part of nine months planning before moving forward with the effort, according to a report published by Mission Local on November 11, 2026.

While some San Francisco Unified School District PTAs raise up to one million dollars a year, schools without them face a stark resource gap. Viz Valley's staff decided to build their own answer rather than wait. Each board member — all teachers or staff at the school — has been personally reaching out to ten friends to solicit donations, using community ties as the seed of a funding base.

The group has drafted a mission statement and is now awaiting official nonprofit status from the IRS, which it expects to receive in early 2027. The plan is not to plug short-term holes like buying classroom supplies for one teacher, but to create sustained, structural support for the school as a whole.

SFUSD's public relations manager, Katrina Kincaide, told Mission Local that SPARK — the district's public foundation — is launching a campaign to support schools that lack a PTA or fundraising structure, suggesting Viz Valley may not be alone in finding new paths to self-sufficiency.

topStories.headline: Hunters Point Community Group Proposes Year-Long Monitoring of AI Data Center on Paul Avenue
topStories.dek: Hunters Point Community Biomonitoring has put forward a pilot proposal to independently measure air quality, noise, heat, and toxic exposure around the Novva data center campus in south-central Bayview–Hunters Point — the first systematic effort to track what the facility may be doing to residents' bodies.
topStories.body:
A community health organization based in Bayview–Hunters Point is pushing for comprehensive, independent monitoring of the Paul Avenue AI data center campus that now operates directly across the street from residential homes. The proposal, announced by Hunters Point Community Biomonitoring in October 2026, calls for a one-year pilot program that would track toxic exposure, air pollution, noise, and heat in the surrounding neighborhood.

The Novva data center at 400 Paul Avenue went through San Francisco's Planning Commission back in 2016, long before many local residents knew the project was under consideration. The facility, which has drawn criticism from community members and researchers, sits in a neighborhood already burdened by a wastewater treatment plant, diesel truck traffic, and industrial operations. Novva has invested $500 million to build a 36-megawatt data center at the site, with the first 9 megawatts coming online in the summer of 2026.

The San Francisco Bay View, which has covered the data center issue extensively, reported on a broader campaign by Oakland and San Francisco organizers fighting data centers they say will drain public resources, pollute Black neighborhoods, and displace jobs. Hunters Point Community Biomonitoring's pilot proposal is a direct attempt to put hard numbers on what, if anything, the facility is doing to the health of residents who live nearby.

The proposal argues that no independent community-wide human biomonitoring program exists that is specifically designed to screen residents adjacent to a facility of this kind for toxic chemicals. If funded and approved, the pilot would become a model for other neighborhoods facing similar industrial encroachments.

topStories.headline: Six-Story Apartment Building Planned for 4101 Third Street in Bayview After Design Revisions
topStories.dek: Updated plans filed this month propose a slimmed-down but still substantial six-story mixed-use building on Third Street, with 45 apartments and ground-floor retail replacing an earlier eight-story design.
topStories.body:
A revised development proposal for 4101 Third Street in Bayview would bring 45 apartments and ground-level retail space to a small infill lot along the neighborhood's main commercial corridor. San Francisco YIMBY reported the updated plans on November 5, 2026 — within the past ten days — noting that the project has been scaled back from an earlier eight-story concept filed in late 2025.

The six-story structure, roughly 65 feet tall, would yield approximately 45,720 square feet of total space, including 39,500 square feet of residential units. The mix consists of 20 one-bedroom and 25 two-bedroom apartments. The ground floor would include about 4,470 square feet of retail. The project provides no vehicle parking but would accommodate 51 bicycles.

The 0.17-acre property sits along Third Street between Innes Avenue, Newhall Street, and Hudson Avenue. Benicia-based NUA Architects is the designer of record, with RKD Consulting serving as engineer. The exterior design calls for full-height bay windows above the ground floor, floor-to-ceiling windows at street level, and a textured concrete facade.

Third Street has been at the center of Bayview's slow commercial revival, drawing Storefront Opportunity Grants and city-funded street markets. The housing proposal adds to that momentum, though it will still need to clear local planning review before construction can begin.

moreNews.headline: Bayview's 3rd Street Gains a New Barbecue Restaurant This Month
moreNews.body: A new barbecue restaurant is expected to open on Third Street in Bayview by mid-November 2026, according to Mission Local's Bayview Buzz column published November 4. The incoming business was awarded a Storefront Opportunity Grant earlier this year. Owner and chef Kimberlee White told Mission Local the restaurant will feature a loyalty program and will be fully up and running around mid-November.
